newsitem.title: USA: Justice Department to push overturn of Prop 209.
newsitem.headline: Justice Department to push overturn of Prop 209.

text.p: The Justice Department has concluded that a California initiative outlawing affirmative action, Proposition 209, is unconstitutional and will back legal action to overturn it, the White House said on Friday.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said President Bill Clinton, who campaigned against the initiative in the Nov. 5 election, fully supported the move.
"Rather than remedying what's wrong with the affirmative action programmes that exist, (Proposition 209) has the effect of abolishing affirmative action," McCurry said.
"The president believes that we need to continue to have that as a tool to remedy discrimination in our society."

Proposition 209, the first initiative of its kind passed by any state, would bar preferential treatment based on race or sex in public employment, education and contracting. It was approved last month by a margin of 54 percent to 46 percent.

Implementation of the initiative is on hold, however. A federal judge earlier this week extended for another week a temporary injunction that is keeping California officials from rolling back affirmative action programmes.

McCurry said the Justice Department would intervene in the case as a plaintiff rather than as a friend of the court. But officials at the department said the form of its intervention had not yet been decided.
Asked how the Clinton administration justified its effort to overrule California voters, McCurry said: "There's always strong preference that goes to the will of the people.
"However, if significant overriding constitutional concern presents itself, the president as the nation's chief constitutional officer has to act to defend the constitution."
